children: Taiwan's inflation climbed to a more than two-year high last month, adding to pressure on the central bank to raise interest rates.

The consumer-price index rose 2.73% in September from a year earlier, above the 2.4% increase expected by economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. That was the island's highest inflation reading since February 2024.
Higher fuel prices and food and electricity costs drove the price increase, the statistics bureau said.
On a month-to-month basis, consumer prices climbed 0.44% from August, Wednesday's data showed.

The latest data complicates the picture for the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), which has held interest rates steady for 10 consecutive quarters despite mounting inflation risks in recent months.

Following the bank's latest policy decision, Gov. Yang Chin-long struck a patient tone, saying that "inflation is still under control, so we have time to wait and see." He added that monetary policy "remains on the tight side for now."
The bank expects inflation to reach 2.03% in 2026 before easing to 1.83% in 2027.
Some economists view that outlook as too sanguine and expect the bank to begin raising rates as early as December, as prolonged U.S.-Iran tensions keep energy prices elevated.
